ZinWaylandIntegration.Goal: The Zin standard library ships a native Wayland client and server implementation generated from canonical Wayland XML during the Stage-0/Stage-1 standard-library bootstrap. Normal Zin projects simply import std.wayland.

BootstrapInput.Location: Stdlib source/bootstrap assets under std/protocols/wayland and/or an equivalent canonical source directory.
BootstrapInput.Rule: Stage-0 or Stage-1 obtains the protocol XML needed to construct the initial std.wayland. Once generated, std.wayland is built as ordinary Zin source/module content.

ImplementationPipeline.Stage: std.xml tokenizer/parser implemented in Zin when Stage-1 capabilities permit
generation/materialization of typed Zin declarations for client and server

ZinWaylandIntegration.Rule: The compiler itself knows modules, comptime, types and reflection. It does not know XML or Wayland semantics.
XML and JSON support are ordinary Zin standard-library modules: std.xml and std.json.

XMLMapping.Interface: Generates typed interface metadata, object proxy/resource types, name and maximum schema version.
XMLMapping.Request: Generates opcode, typed client request method, server decode/dispatch metadata.
XMLMapping.Event: Generates opcode, typed server event method, client decode/dispatch metadata.
XMLMapping.Arg: wl.Fixed, signed 24.8 value represented by i32
nullable or non-null UTF-8 byte slice according to allow-null; wire includes trailing NUL and 4-byte padding
typed object reference/proxy/resource according to interface and nullability
typed created object identity; generic new_id follows Wayland interface/version metadata rules
wl.ArrayView raw byte slice with Wayland alignment
wl.Handle transported out of band by the transport backend
XMLMapping.Enum: Generated protocol enum values use explicit integer backing and exact XML values. Bitfield enums use std.wayland flag helpers without operator overloading.

WireProtocol.Header: Wayland object id plus packed message size/opcode header exactly according to the Wayland wire protocol.
WireProtocol.Strings: Length includes trailing NUL and byte payload is padded to 4-byte boundary.
WireProtocol.Arrays: Length prefix plus bytes padded to 4-byte boundary.
WireProtocol.Handles: Descriptors/handles are associated out-of-band in message order and are not serialized as integer payload fields.
WireProtocol.ObjectIds: u32 connection-local identifiers; zero means null only where allowed.

ZinWaylandIntegration.Client: std.wayland.client provides connection, object ID allocation, request marshaling, handle transfer, event decode/dispatch, delete-id handling, object version gating and protocol-error handling.
ZinWaylandIntegration.Server: std.wayland.server provides display/listener, clients, globals/registry, resources, request decode/dispatch, event send, handle transfer, object version gating and protocol-error handling.

Transport.Linux: Native Zin Linux Unix-domain transport, ancillary descriptor transfer, shared memory and waiting primitives.
Transport.BSD: Native Zin BSD Unix-domain transport, ancillary descriptor transfer, shared memory and poll/kqueue-compatible waiting primitives.
Transport.Brix: brixOS native local IPC and shared-memory primitives may be used directly as long as they preserve Wayland message ordering, peer lifecycle, handle transfer and shared-memory semantics. brixOS kernel internals need not be POSIX.

Conformance.Rule: Opcode numbers, argument order/types, nullability, since-version rules, destructor semantics and enum values match the input XML exactly.
Generated client and server declarations from the same XML are wire-compatible with established Wayland implementations.
Both client and server APIs are available through std.wayland without project build configuration.
